Package org.unitseek.knitid.generator.ksid

Record Class KsidConfig

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.unitseek.knitid.generator.ksid.KsidConfig
Record Components:
epoch - timestamp epoch; the default is 2018-11-16T00:00:00Z
timestampBits - timestamp width; must fit within 42 bits
datacenterIdBits - datacenter id width
workerIdBits - worker id width
sequenceBits - per-millisecond sequence width
clockBackwardsStrategy - behaviour when the clock moves backwards
maxBackwardsWait - upper bound for wait-based clock catch-up
sequenceOverflowStrategy - behaviour when the sequence is exhausted
allowBorrowFuture - explicit opt-in for BORROW_FUTURE
leaseRenewInterval - WorkerId lease renewal interval
leaseMaxRenewFailures - consecutive renewal failures before the lease is marked invalid
public record KsidConfig(Instant epoch, int timestampBits, int datacenterIdBits, int workerIdBits, int sequenceBits, ClockBackwardsStrategy clockBackwardsStrategy, Duration maxBackwardsWait, SequenceOverflowStrategy sequenceOverflowStrategy, boolean allowBorrowFuture, Duration leaseRenewInterval, int leaseMaxRenewFailures) extends Record
Immutable KSID configuration.

Layout: 1 sign bit (always 0) + timestamp bits + datacenter bits + worker bits + sequence bits = 64 bits, therefore the four configurable fields must sum to 63.

Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • defaults

      public static KsidConfig defaults()
      Returns the default KSID configuration.

      41 timestamp bits, 5 datacenter bits, 5 worker bits, 12 sequence bits, WAIT strategies and a 20-second lease renewal interval.

      default KSID configuration
